PTSD in the human brain · Nature 2025 · try it

From open chromatin to genes and risk variants

Hwang, Skarica, Xu et al. measured gene expression and open chromatin in more than two million nuclei from the prefrontal cortex of 111 donors with PTSD, depression or neither. Two of the ideas behind the study, on small simulated data: linking a stretch of open chromatin to the gene it controls, and using those elements to find which variant at a risk locus is likely causal. Boxes marked Paper quote the paper.

A peak that opens when the gene is on is a candidate regulatory element

CRE: r(accessibility of the peak, expression of the gene) > 0.4 and FDR < 0.05, across groups of similar nuclei

Single-nucleus ATAC sequencing finds the peaks of open chromatin around a gene; paired expression data say when the gene is on. Where a peak’s accessibility rises and falls with the gene’s expression across groups of nuclei, the two are linked, and the peak counts as a candidate regulatory element (CRE). Tap a peak to see its scatter; move the threshold.

Paper 913,717 peaks of open chromatin. With six high-quality samples measured both ways, 1,433,145 peak-to-gene links (r > 0.45, FDR < 10−4); peaks with a link at r > 0.4 and FDR < 0.05 give 395,932 cell-type-specific CREs. Almost every PTSD gene in endothelial cells (544 of 585) and in excitatory neurons (313 of 322) has one. The links of FKBP5, the stress-hormone gene that rises most in endothelial cells, with r > 0.75 all come from endothelial and microglial CREs (Fig. 4; links computed with ArchR, up to 2 Mb away).

Toy: 300 groups of similar nuclei from four cell types (excitatory and inhibitory neurons, endothelial cells, astrocytes) and 12 peaks in a 400 kb window. The gene’s expression is driven by its promoter and three enhancers; the other peaks only follow their own cell types. FDR: Benjamini–Hochberg over the window’s 12 tests.

Which variant at a risk locus is causal? Let open chromatin weigh in

PIPj ∝ πj · BFj,   πj = the CRE’s peak score (1–100) if SNP j lies in one, 0.1 otherwise

Variants close together are inherited together (linkage disequilibrium, LD), so a GWAS gives many of them similar evidence, and the strongest signal need not be the cause. Fine-mapping turns the evidence into a posterior inclusion probability (PIP) for each variant. The study weighted variants that sit in cell-type CREs, so that a variant in an element active in the right cells gains weight. Switch the annotation, draw new GWAS samples, tap a variant.

Paper At MAD1L1, the strongest variant in the Million Veteran Program GWAS, rs10235664, has PIP 0.01 once inhibitory-neuron CREs are used; rs62444919, in high LD with it (r = 0.84) and inside such a CRE, reaches 0.36 and loops to the promoter of a neighbouring gene, ELFN1 (link correlations 0.87 and 0.67). A previously reported causal variant for KCNIP4, rs4697248, is confirmed in excitatory neurons (PIP 0.93). Method: SuSiE on the GWAS summary statistics, LD from 503 European samples of 1000 Genomes, prior weights from peak scores (−log10 P, capped at the 95th percentile, rescaled to 1–100) and 0.1 outside peaks (Fig. 5c–d, Methods).

Toy: 40 SNPs in 300 kb, genotypes for 503 simulated people with one block of strong LD; one causal SNP inside an inhibitory-neuron CRE that loops to gene 2. z-scores are drawn as z ~ N(λ R·c, R) with λ = 6.2; PIPs use one single effect (SuSiE with L = 1) and Wakefield’s approximate Bayes factor. Color: r2 with the selected SNP.

Toys, not results: small simulated data computed with the study’s definitions. Study: Hwang, Skarica, Xu et al., Nature 643, 744–754 (2025).
